html:
The Northern Paiute are a Numic people of the western Great Basin, in what is now eastern California, western Nevada and southeast Oregon. They call themselves Numu.

Their way of life fitted a harsh desert. Each band held a territory, usually around a lake or marsh that gave fish and waterfowl. Bands joined for communal hunts of rabbits and pronghorn, and gathered pinyon nuts in the mountains in autumn as a key winter food. Their language is close to that of the Shoshone and the Bannock.

Settlers, miners and ranchers arrived from the 1840s. In 1860 the Pyramid Lake War broke out in Nevada. The writer Sarah Winnemucca spoke and wrote for her people in the 1880s, and the Northern Paiute prophet Wovoka began the Ghost Dance in 1889. Today Northern Paiute people live on many reservations and colonies, some shared with the Shoshone, and some at Warm Springs in Oregon.
